record.original_question: For a domain D in C, define ρ(x, y) = sup{|f (x) − f (y)| : x, y ∈ D; f analytic in D; |f ′ | ≤ 1 in D}. If D is convex, then ρ(x, y) = |x − y|, but not otherwise. Clearly ρ(x, y) ≤ L(x, y), the infimum of the lengths of paths in G that join x to y. What can be said about ρ for general D, in terms of the geometry of D? (L. A. Rubel)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain (a connected open subset of the complex plane). For points $x, y \in D$, define
$$\rho(x,y) = \sup\bigl\{\,|f(x) - f(y)| : f \text{ is holomorphic on } D \text{ with } |f'(z)| \le 1 \text{ for all } z \in D\,\bigr\}.$$
For $x, y \in D$, also let
$$L(x,y) = \inf\bigl\{\,\operatorname{length}(\gamma) : \gamma \text{ is a rectifiable path in } D \text{ from } x \text{ to } y\,\bigr\}$$
be the inner (geodesic) distance in $D$.

It is known that $\rho(x,y) \le L(x,y)$ always, and that if $D$ is convex then $\rho(x,y) = |x-y|$. It is also known that this equality $\rho(x,y) = |x-y|$ can fail for non-convex $D$.

Problem. Describe $\rho(x,y)$ for a general domain $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ in terms of the geometry of $D$. In particular, give a geometric characterization, formula, or sharp two-sided estimate for $\rho(x,y)$ in terms of geometric/metric quantities of $D$ (such as Euclidean distance, inner length distance, distance to the boundary, or the convex hull structure of $D$).
artifact.category_tag: Extremal problems for bounded-derivative analytic functions
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution of Rubel's question characterizing the extremal pseudodistance $\rho$ on a general planar domain in terms of the geometry of the domain was located. The problem appears in a well-known list of function-theoretic research problems and its current status is not clearly documented in accessible sources.
